pr_title: TSDB: Fix time series bounds default value error
pr_body:
Adds support for default start and end dates that includes entire range of dates that we can parse from year -9999 to year 9999. That should simplify the onboarding experience since if a user doesn't use datastreams they get a single index that covers all time ranges. 

Fixes #82832

Co-authored-by: weizijun <weizijun1989@gmail.com>

issue_context.title: TSDB: Confusing error message for start/end dates
comments: Let me take a look at this exception
I fixed the exception in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/82851, and push another PR to add more check: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/82847

> at all and use their default values when missing?

The more I am thinking about it the more I like that. This will simplify things and we probably don't care about the dates when we create a single index anyway, they are an important part of datastream story, but probably not here.

review_comments: Are `IndexSettings.TIME_SERIES_START_TIME` and `IndexSettings.TIME_SERIES_END_TIME` not required in the time_series index? I added the checking code to make these settings required. This is a requirement for the time_series index before. Now remove the check will change the requirement.  I think it's ok to make these settings not required, but we should check that if it satisfies the design of time_series index.
They are no longer required, but if they are not there we just use the default values.
It looks like if you leave it blank he's got it configured to cover -9999 to 9999. I wasn't super keen on having defaults for these a few months ago, but I suppose it's fine.
My preference would be to support an entire range from Long.MIN_VALUE to Long.MAX_VALUE but we are not capable of parsing such dates. This is the entire range we can parse.
